title: Zoom in: a presigned multipart upload, from request to event
caption: The API is called twice (start and complete); everything in between is the client and the store.

messages.label: POST /uploads {600 MB, video/mp4}
messages.note: The app says what it intends to upload; the API checks quota and allowed types.

messages.label: INSERT video v_77 (pending)
messages.note: The id is random, so keys spread evenly across the store.

messages.label: start multipart: videos/v_77/original
messages.note: The store returns an upload id for this one key.

messages.label: upload id + 60 part URLs
messages.note: Each URL is signed for one part number of one key, valid for 1 hour.

messages.label: PUT parts 1–60 (10 MB, 6 at a time)
messages.note: Parallel parts use all the bandwidth; a failed part is resent alone.

messages.label: ETag per part
messages.note: The client keeps the list.

messages.label: POST /uploads/v_77/complete [ETags]
messages.note: Second and last API call.

messages.label: complete multipart
messages.note: The store stitches the parts into one object atomically: readers never see half a file.

messages.label: ObjectCreated videos/v_77/original
messages.note: Processing starts from the event, not from the API call.

scenarios.name: Event lost or late
scenarios.summary: Store notifications are at-least-once and occasionally late; a sweeper keeps a video from staying pending forever.

messages.label: POST /uploads/v_77/complete
messages.note: The upload itself went fine.

messages.label: complete multipart
messages.note: The object exists.

messages.label: ObjectCreated v_77
messages.note: This notification is delayed for an hour.

messages.label: sweeper: pending > 10 min?
messages.note: A periodic job looks for rows that should have been processed by now.

messages.label: HEAD videos/v_77/original
messages.note: The object is there, so it was the event that went missing, not the upload.

messages.label: enqueue v_77 again
messages.note: Workers are idempotent by key; if the late event also arrives, the second run is a no-op.

scenarios.name: Complete sent twice
scenarios.summary: The app's complete call times out and is retried: the API treats an already-uploaded video as success.

messages.label: complete [ETags]
messages.note: First call.

messages.label: complete multipart
messages.note: Succeeds.

messages.label: UPDATE v_77 SET status = uploaded
messages.note: Recorded.
Lost on the network.

messages.label: complete [ETags] (retry)
messages.note: Same video id.

messages.label: status already uploaded
messages.note: The upload id no longer exists in the store, but the row says the work is done.

messages.label: 200 (same answer)
messages.note: Retry-safe: no error and no second object.

scenarios.name: Risk: wrong file
scenarios.summary: A client claims a 600 MB video and sends a 4 GB executable; conditions in the signature and a check in the worker stop it.

messages.label: POST /uploads {600 MB, video/mp4}
messages.note: What the client claims.

messages.label: URLs with size and type conditions
messages.note: The signature pins content-type and a content-length range.

messages.label: PUT 4 GB with another type
messages.note: Doesn't match what was signed.

messages.label: 403 signature mismatch
messages.note: Rejected before it is stored.

messages.label: ObjectCreated (a file that passed)
messages.note: Anything that does get in is checked again downstream.

messages.label: worker: magic bytes not video → rejected
messages.note: Never trust the extension: the worker sniffs the content, quarantines it and marks the row rejected.
